clue.text: Men of letter are low on alcohol: Royal Academy take note!

parts.note: lite is the commercial spelling for a drink with reduced alcohol or calories
standard abbreviation for the Royal Academy of Arts
ti (or te) is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Writers are warned off drink, and the Royal Academy is told to pay attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take note!' reads as an instruction, but 'take' just joins the sol-fa note to the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The literati are educated, literary people, so 'men of letters' is a direct synonym phrase.

clue.text: Never mind where pests are hiding

indicators.note: 'where ... are hiding' says the target is concealed inside the words just named
hiding means sitting unseen within the preceding phrase, spread across its words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of never and the start of mind

explanation.surface: A shrug of indifference about where the household pests have got to.
explanation.definitionFit: Vermin are animals such as rats and mice regarded as harmful nuisances, i.e. pests.

clue.text: Person is, to a T, a "people person"

parts.note: a person is a human
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone described as being exactly, 'to a T', a sociable type who likes other people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To a T' is an idiom for 'exactly', but here the T is simply a letter added on.
explanation.definitionFit: A humanist puts human beings and their welfare at the centre of things, so is playfully a believer in people.

clue.text: Salt dosage is incorrect

indicators.note: something incorrect is wrong, so the letters before it are not in their right order

parts.note: the six letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A complaint that the amount of salt prescribed or added is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salt' looks like a seasoning in a recipe, but it is the old slang for an experienced sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: An old salt and a sea dog are both informal terms for a seasoned, weathered sailor.

clue.text: Compelled one to leave drive-in

indicators.note: leaving means going away, so that letter departs from the word that follows

parts.note: a drive-in is a cinema watched from your car; hyphen ignored
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone forced to walk out of a drive-in cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: Being driven means being pushed or forced to act, so it is a synonym of compelled.

clue.text: Tyrant''s in Regimental HQ

indicators.note: in places the possessive ending inside the headquarters word

parts.note: a depot is a regiment's headquarters and training base
the S of the possessive ending

explanation.surface: The dictator is said to be holed up in the army's headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s seems to belong to the tyrant, but it supplies the letter S.
explanation.definitionFit: A despot is a ruler with absolute power who uses it cruelly, a close synonym for a tyrant.

clue.text: Government measures

definitions.meaning: first meaning: those who govern a country
second meaning: straight-edged strips for measuring lengths

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a phrase about policies a government introduces; really it is two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural noun means both the people in power and the marked strips used for measuring length.

clue.text: Speak about German conjunction for a period of 24 hours

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the speaking word wraps round what follows

parts.note: to speak is to say
und is German for 'and', a conjunction

explanation.surface: An instruction to talk about German grammar for a whole day.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunday, like every day of the week, lasts twenty-four hours, so this definition is by example.

clue.text: Perhaps Blair, partly dropping Left, gets advantage over moderate centre

indicators.note: dropping means letting go of, so that letter falls out of the word before it

parts.note: taken as written
L is the standard abbreviation for left
a lead is an advantage over rivals

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle, so only its middle letters are used

parts.note: the two middle letters of this eight-letter word

explanation.surface: Tony Blair drifting from the left and winning by occupying the moderate centre ground, i.e. New Labour.
explanation.walkthrough: Tony Blair led the UK Labour Party; 'Perhaps' marks him as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Tony Blair headed the Labour Party, so he is one example of a politician at the head of a political group.

clue.text: Egghead hunts round for respect

indicators.note: the head of a word is its front, so only the first letter is kept

parts.note: the head, or first letter, of egg

indicators.note: turning round sends the word back the other way

parts.note: in fox hunting, the gatherings of riders and hounds are called meets

explanation.surface: An intellectual searching about for some respect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egghead' looks like one word for an intellectual, but it is split into egg plus its head.
explanation.definitionFit: Esteem is high regard or admiration for someone, a near synonym of respect as a noun.

clue.text: Leaves Bonn a sad mess

indicators.note: a mess is disorder, so the preceding letters are jumbled up

parts.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone departs from Bonn, finding the former German capital a depressing mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like the verb 'departs', which it is, but not in the way the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon a place or person is to leave them behind for good, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: You almost start to grasp a Hindu system of philosophy

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, which alone is taken

parts.note: first letter of grasp
taken as written

explanation.surface: Encouragement that you are nearly beginning to understand an Indian philosophy.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoga is one of the six orthodox schools of Hindu thought, of which the postures are only a part.

clue.text: Say, not Thatcher's Sir Bernard seen in Midlands city!

indicators.note: say means speak the next word aloud and write down a name that matches its sound

parts.note: John Nott was Defence Secretary in Margaret Thatcher's government
Sir Bernard Ingham was Thatcher's press secretary

explanation.surface: A denial that Thatcher's famous spokesman was ever spotted in a Midlands city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thatcher's' does double duty: both Nott and Ingham served under Margaret Thatcher, UK Prime Minister 1979-90.
explanation.definitionFit: Nottingham is a major city in the East Midlands region of England, home of Robin Hood legend.

clue.text: Tickling breast: euphoria is said to follow!

parts.note: tit is slang for a breast

indicators.note: is said means the word is only heard, so a spelling with the same sound is used

parts.note: elation is euphoria; run on after the slang word, it is heard with an unstressed first vowel

explanation.surface: A cheeky note that touching someone's chest leads to bliss.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken together, the slang word plus 'elation' sounds like the answer, which is spelt differently.
explanation.definitionFit: Titillation is pleasurable excitement or stimulation, and in its older literal sense it means tickling.

clue.text: Fashionable opinion, for example

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'
a stance is a stated position or opinion

explanation.surface: A trendy view offered as an illustration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For example' looks like a phrase tacked on the end, but 'example' alone is the definition, linked by 'for'.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is a single case cited to illustrate something, which is what an example is.

clue.text: Someone conscientious in wartime, perhaps

parts.note: surface reading: a diligent, dutiful person during a war
setter's reading: the word completes a fixed phrase for someone refusing military service on moral grounds

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as praise for a hard worker; the trick is that 'conscientious' goes with the answer to form a familiar phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A conscientious objector refuses to fight in a war for reasons of conscience; 'perhaps' shows this is one kind of the answer.

clue.text: Introspectively , found oneself unaccomplished

indicators.note: looking inward means the answer is found inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run from inside found across into oneself

explanation.surface: On reflection, someone discovers they have achieved nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Work that is undone has not been carried out or finished, so it is unaccomplished.

clue.text: Faculty has to spend a penny in school

indicators.note: in puts the first piece inside the abbreviation that follows

parts.note: standard abbreviation for school
'spend a penny' is a British euphemism for urinating, from old coin-operated public toilets

explanation.surface: A university faculty needs to use the toilet while at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Faculty' suggests a university department, but here it means a mental or physical power.
explanation.definitionFit: Speech is one of the human faculties, the natural ability to talk, like the faculty of sight.

clue.text: Express in restrained terms, being less than articulate

parts.note: under means less than, as in 'under ten'
to articulate is to state or express clearly

explanation.surface: Someone who plays things down by not quite managing to speak clearly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articulate' looks like an adjective meaning eloquent; it is the verb meaning to put into words.
explanation.definitionFit: To understate is to describe something as smaller or less serious than it is, using deliberately modest language.

clue.text: Breaks out in purest mayhem

indicators.note: mayhem is wild chaos, so the preceding word's letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the six letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Something erupts into the most complete chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: A volcano or a quarrel that erupts bursts out suddenly and violently, so the verbs match.

clue.text: Prue returns accepting honour for a Brussels politician

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the name holds the honour inside it
returning means going back, so the name is read from its end to its start

parts.note: taken as written
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A woman named Prue comes back having accepted an honour for being a European politician.
explanation.walkthrough: The Order of Merit is an honour given by the British monarch; MEP means Member of the European Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: A Euro-MP sits in the European Parliament, which meets partly in Brussels, so the description fits.

clue.text: Japan loses one, but gets English joke

indicators.note: losing something means it is gone, so those letters drop out of the country

parts.note: taken as written
an is the indefinite article, meaning one
standard abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Japan is beaten in a match but enjoys an English joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' here is the word an, not the usual I or A.
explanation.definitionFit: A jape is a practical joke or prank, an old-fashioned but standard synonym.

clue.text: The common people's music: a clue, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints the letters could be arranged some other way

parts.note: pop is popular music
these five letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Pop music presented as the music of ordinary folk, offered as a hint.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s looks possessive, but it stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The populace is the general mass of people in a country, as opposed to the elite.

clue.text: Stone alien spaceship

parts.note: a stone is a rock
ET, the extra-terrestrial from the film, is the crossword alien

explanation.surface: A spacecraft built of rock and flown by extra-terrestrials.
explanation.definitionFit: A rocket is a vehicle propelled by rocket engines into space, so it is a spaceship.

clue.text: Sent first of suitors off with cool allure

indicators.note: off means removed, so that letter is taken away from the word it heads

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: first of picks out only the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: first letter of suitors
to ice is to cool, as with a drink

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses their admirers with a cool attraction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent ... off' reads as a phrasal verb about dismissing suitors; really it removes a letter from sent.
explanation.definitionFit: To allure is to attract or tempt someone, and to entice is to lure with a promise of pleasure.

clue.text: Sadomasochism has pair tentatively hitting, initially without roughness

parts.note: SM is the standard abbreviation for sadomasochism
a pair of O-shaped letters, two rings side by side

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so each word gives only its opening letter

parts.note: first letters of each word

explanation.surface: A racy scene of a couple trying out gentle blows, with nothing rough about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something smooth has an even, regular surface or manner, free of bumps or harshness.
